newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Insurer Winterthur sees stable China.
newsitem.headline: Insurer Winterthur sees stable China.

text.p: Winterthur Swiss Insurance Co, the first European insurer to operate in China, said on Thursday it expected conditions there for foreign businesses to remain unchanged after the death of paramount ruler Deng Xiaoping.
"We are quite confident that things will go on as they are at the moment," said Joern Kristensen, managing director of Winterthur China, speaking by telephone from his Shanghai office.

Winterthur launched its Shanghai-based subsidiary in December after winning a licence for non-life business a month earlier, the first European to join a growing handful of foreign insurers allowed to operate in China.
Kristensen said Winterthur believed China would continue the economic reform policies forged by Deng that include an opening to investment and operation by Western companies.
"We think these things have been solved over the past years more or less to prepare for the post-Deng era," he said.
"We feel the situation is quite stable and we don't expect any dramatic developments," he added.

Winterthur's China subsidiary has a working capital of 120 million yuan. China's insurance market once was virtually monopolised by the state-owned People's Insurance Group but the sector is now gradually opening up to domestic as well as foreign competition.

Besides Winterthur, companies able to write insurance policies in China include American International Assurance Co Ltd, which is part of the American International Group, Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd and a Hong Kong unit of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co of Canada, which has a joint venture life insurance operation.
